scenes.headline: Classes & Object-Oriented Design
scenes.subtitle: Modeling data and behavior together
scenes.narration: Classes bundle state and behavior into a single unit, letting you model pipeline components as reusable, testable objects rather than sprawling collections of loose functions.

scenes.headline: Anatomy of a class
items: Methods are functions on the class
scenes.narration: The __init__ method runs automatically at construction and is where you establish each object's starting state. The self parameter is how every method reaches back to its own object's data. Methods are simply functions that live on the class and operate through self. And the distinction between class attributes, shared by all instances, and instance attributes, unique to each object, is a common source of subtle bugs worth understanding early.

scenes.headline: Defining a class
scenes.narration: In this Extractor, source and rows are instance state established when the object is built. The load method reads from that source and stores the result back on the instance through self, then returns a count. Any code holding an Extractor can now call load and query its rows, with the object carrying its own data along the way.

scenes.headline: Inheritance vs composition
scenes.narration: Inheritance models an is-a relationship, where a subclass genuinely is a specialized kind of its base and extends its behavior. Composition instead models a has-a relationship, where an object holds other objects and delegates to them. Composition tends to be more flexible and less brittle, so prefer it when in doubt, and reserve inheritance for cases where the is-a relationship is truly natural.

scenes.headline: Inheritance & dunders
scenes.narration: CsvExtractor inherits from Extractor and overrides load with CSV-specific parsing while keeping everything else. The __repr__ dunder method controls how the object appears when printed or logged, integrating it cleanly with Python's built-in tooling. Well-chosen dunders let your objects behave like native types.

scenes.headline: Encapsulation conventions
scenes.narration: A single leading underscore is a convention signaling an attribute is internal and shouldn't be relied on externally. A double underscore triggers name mangling, which helps avoid accidental clashes in subclasses. The property decorator exposes a computed value as if it were a plain attribute. And classmethod and staticmethod define methods bound to the class rather than to any single instance.

scenes.headline: Object lifecycle
scenes.narration: You define a class once, then instantiate it as many times as you need. Each object lives while you call its methods and hold a reference to it. Once no references remain, the object becomes eligible for garbage collection and its memory is reclaimed.

scenes.text: Encapsulate state, favor composition over inheritance, and use @property instead of getter methods.
scenes.narration: Clean object-oriented design keeps state well encapsulated, composes small pieces over deep hierarchies, and exposes computed values through properties rather than verbose getters.
